nodes.name: Mo-PBA/NFF
aliases: Mo-doped Prussian blue analogs on NiFe foam

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Hydrothermally prepared Mo-doped Prussian blue analogs (PBAs) with Fe2O3 byproducts were used as precursors. After a simple hydrothermal reaction at 140°C, Mo-PBA/NFF as the templating precursor was first in situ synthesized on NiFe alloy foam, which served as the self-supporting substrate and nickel sources simultaneously. The color of NFF skeletons changed from the initial metallic silver to pale blue. A mixture of abundant NiFe-PBA nanoblocks and flowerlike Fe2O3 byproducts can be observed.
nodes.source_text: The hydrothermally prepared Mo-doped Prussian blue analogs (PBAs) with Fe2O3 byproducts were used as precursors... After a simple hydrothermal reaction, Mo-PBA/NFF as the templating precursor was first in situ synthesized on NiFe alloy foam...

nodes.name: Air calcination
nodes.procedure: After subsequent air calcination at 400°C, the original morphology was still maintained, but cracks appeared in the NiFe-PBA nanoblocks and Fe2O3 nanoflower, and the sample turned light yellow.
nodes.source_text: After subsequent calcination, the original morphology was still maintained...

nodes.name: Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: Finally, the phosphorization process produced by PH3 vapor from the decomposition of NaH2PO2, H2O successfully constructed the interface between Ni2P and FexP and formed a porous 3D network nanostructure, resulting in the dark blue Mo-Ni2P/FexP-V/NFF catalysts.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting (OWS) in alkaline two-electrode electrolyzer
nodes.source_text: the OWS was further investigated with self-supported Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V/NFF electrodes served as both cathode and anode in a two-electrode electrolyzer... the Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V/NFF||Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V/NFF electrolyzer affording current densities of 10 and 100mAcm⁻² only required 1.49 and 1.74V, respectively... the current densities at 1.49 and 1.69V underwent a negligible decline for 20h

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals surface reconstruction with fractured nanoblocks and nanoflowers forming thick cracked layer of small nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: after phosphorization treatment... the original nanoblock and nanoflower are all fractured and collapsed, transforming into a thick layer with many cracks, consisting of small nanoparticles with uneven sizes, as shown in Figure 1d

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows porous nanoparticle structure advantageous for mass transport.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM analysis... revealing the porous structure of Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V layer composed of a large number of nanoparticles, which was advantageous to faster mass transport and exposure of more active sites

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms triphasic Fe₂P-Ni₂P-FeP heterostructure and reveals P vacancies observed as circled regions in images.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1f shows the HR-TEM images... implying the nature of a triphasic Fe₂P-Ni₂P-FeP heterostructure... As shown by circles in Figure 1f, anionic P vacancies can be observed in the HRTEM images.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows well-defined rings indexed to (111) planes of Ni₂P and Fe₂P, and (211) plane of FeP, confirming polycrystalline heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the well-defined rings in SAED pattern could be indexed to the (111), (111), and (211) planes of Ni₂P, Fe₂P, and FeP, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, P, and Mo elements throughout the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping of Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V revealed the presence of Ni, Fe, P, and Mo elements uniformly distributed throughout the entire surface...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of Ni₂P (JCPDS 03-0953), Fe₂P (JCPDS 27-1171), and FeP (JCPDS 71-2262), confirming mixed phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Among the XRD peaks of Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V, three sets of characteristic peaks associated with Ni₂P (JCPDS 03-0953), Fe₂P (JCPDS 27-1171), and FeP (JCPDS 71-2262)... could be clearly observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows characteristic Ni-P and Fe-P bond peaks at 594 and 690 cm⁻¹ (Fe-O); peaks shift to lower energy after Mo doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the characteristic peaks attributed to Ni-P bond coexist with the peaks of Fe-P bond... the remaining peaks located at 594 and 690 cm⁻¹ might be assigned to Fe-O bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows prominent signal at g=2.005 indicating P vacancies; stronger signal for Mo-doped sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectrum of Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V is displayed in Figure 2c, revealing a prominent signal at g = 2.005 and indicating the presence of anion P vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Ni (Ni²⁺ at 856.3/874.2 eV, Niδ⁺ at 852.9/870.1 eV), Fe (Fe-P at 706.8/719.7 eV, Fe²⁺, Fe³⁺), Mo (Mo⁶⁺ at 232.4/235.7 eV), P (P 2p at 129.2/130.1 eV); peak shifts indicate Mo-Ni/Fe electron interactions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution XPS spectra of Ni 2p could be fitted with three sets of peaks associated with Ni²⁺... Niδ⁺ in the Ni-P bonds... Mo 3d spectrum... peaks located at 232.4 and 235.7 eV belong to Mo 3d₅/₂ and Mo 3d₃/₂ of Mo⁶⁺...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge between Ni and NiO, shifts higher after Mo doping; Fe K-edge shows deep phosphidation lower valence than FeO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2d, the valence state of Ni... between Ni and NiO. After the molybdenum is doped, the K-edge spectrum of Ni shifts to higher energies... Figure 2g, Ni₂P/FeₓP-V and Mo—Ni₂P/FeₓP-V samples show deep phosphidation features with lower valence than that of FeO

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge: Ni-P at 1.5 Å shortened after Mo doping; Fe K-edge: Fe-O/P at ~1.4 Å distance increased by Mo doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e... peak at 1.5 Å corresponds to Ni-P bond. The shortening of Ni-P bond in Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V... Figure 2h... major peak ≈1.4 Å ascribed to Fe—O/P bonds... peaks related to Fe—O/P bonds shift negatively compared with Mo-doped

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of 6.294 m²/g; BJH pore size centered at 6.478 nm indicating mesoporous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface areas of Mo-PBA/NFF, MoPBA/NFF-C, Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V/NFF are determined to be 6.645, 8.495 and 6.294 m²g⁻¹, respectively... pore size distributions... centered at ∼7.959, 9.222, and 6.478 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman at 0.6 V vs Hg/HgO shows peaks at 470, 551 cm⁻¹ (NiOOH) and 671 cm⁻¹ (FeOOH), confirming oxyhydroxides as OER active species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: when the potential increased to 0.6 V vs Hg/HgO... peaks ≈470 and 551 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the E_g bending vibration and the A_{lg} stretching vibration modes of Ni-O in NiOOH... Raman band at 671 cm⁻¹ is attributed to the F-O vibrations of FeOOH...

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates gives Cdl = 22.6 mF cm⁻², highest among samples indicating largest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V presented the largest C_dl value of 22.6 mF cm⁻², which was much larger than the others, indicating that it possessed more exposed active sites

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smallest semicircle (lowest Rct) for Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V confirming fastest charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Nyquist diagram... revealed that Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V exhibited the smallest semicircle diameter, indicating that the charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of Mo-Ni₂P/FeₓP-V was smaller
